Before
 Hon'Ble Shri Justice G. S. Ahluwalia
 On The 6 th Of November, 2025
 Miscellaneous Second Appeal No. 14 of 2024
 Banshi Dhakad And Others
 Versus
 The State Of Madhya Pradesh
 Appearance:
Mr. Bhupendra Singh Dhakad - Advocate for appellants.

Mr. Dilip Awasthi - Govt. Advocate for respondent / Sta
 Judgment

This miscellaneous second appeal has been filed under Section 71(6) of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 against the judgment and decree dated 14/8/2024 passed by the Food Safety Appellate Tribunal cum First District Judge, District Morena, in MCA No. 33/2024, by which the appeal filed by appellants was partly allowed, and the order dated 4/3/2024 passed by the Additional District Magistrate cum Adjudicating Officer, District Morena, in Case No.
30/2020/Food Safety was modified, and total penalty of Rs. 2,00,000/-, imposed against appellant No. 1, was reduced to Rs. 1,40,000, total penalty of Rs. 4,00,000/-, imposed against appellant No. 2,
was also reduced to Rs. 1,40,000.

entities.text: Food Safety Appellate Tribunal cum First District Judge, District Morena
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. Records of both the Courts below have been received.
3. A solitary ground was raised by counsel for appellants that although the appellants had filed their reply to the show-cause notice, but their defense has not been taken into consideration.

4. From the order sheets of the court of the Adjudicating Officer, it is clear that the prosecution closed its evidence on 17/1/2024, and the case was fixed for NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-GWL:28226 2 MSA-14-2024 6/2/2024 for examination of defense witnesses.
On 6/2/2024, the case was adjourned at the request of counsel for appellants.

On 22/2/2024, counsel Banshi Dhakad vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 6 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/130915989/
1 for appellants expressed his inability to produce any defense witness, and accordingly, the right of appellants to lead defense evidence was closed.
5.

entities.text: Banshi Dhakad vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 6 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Under these circumstances, it is clear that in spite of the opportunity granted by the Adjudicating Officer, appellants did not lead any evidence in their defense.

Therefore, this Court is of considered opinion that the submission made by counsel for appellants that the appellants were not granted sufficient opportunity to defend themselves is misconceived and cannot be accepted.

6. Since no other argument has been advanced, accordingly, judgment and decree dated 14/8/2024 passed by the Food Safety Appellate Tribunal cum First District Judge, District Morena, in MCA No.
33/2024, and order dated 4/3/2024 passed by the Additional District Magistrate cum Adjudicating Officer, Morena, in Case No. 30/2020/Food Safety, are hereby affirmed.

entities.text: Food Safety Appellate Tribunal cum First District Judge, District Morena
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 7. This miscellaneous second appeal fails and is hereby dismissed.

(G. S. AHLUWALIA) JUDGE AKS Banshi Dhakad vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 6 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/130915989/
